components.source_compared: PTE5 p. 244: definition for any collection; remark sup E|X_i| <= M+1 < infinity; dominated example.
components.gap: Preserve the source variant of the definition. Durrett (PTE5, p. 244) defines uniform integrability for an arbitrary collection of random variables X_i, i in I, with no integrability assumed, and remarks that choosing M with the supremum below 1 gives sup_i E|X_i| <= M+1 < infinity; under that definition integrability of every member is a consequence, not a hypothesis. def:p15-uniform-integrability (body 15-35) defines the notion only for families of real integrable random variables, and the bound E|X_i| <= M+1 (annex 6-7) is derived only for such families. The arbitrary-collection form, and the fact that uniform integrability forces integrability (a collection with a non-integrable member is not uniformly integrable), are not supplied on the route: a narrowed variant.

components.gap: Supply Theorem 4.6.2 in its source form (PTE5, p. 245): for any phi >= 0 with phi(x)/x -> infinity (examples x^p with p > 1 and x log+ x) and E phi(|X_i|) <= C for all i, the collection {X_i} is uniformly integrable, with no integrability of the X_i assumed (integrability is a consequence of the moment bound), and the source's statement that this is a common way to check uniform integrability. thm:p15-ui-moment-criteria (body 48-61) states the criterion for 'the family' of def:p15-uniform-integrability, whose members are presupposed integrable, and only for finite Borel Phi; its proof (annex 36-46) never derives integrability from the moment bound. The source's weaker hypothesis is therefore not preserved (narrowed variant), and the framing sentence is absent.

defect_observations: Adaptedness: def:p15-filtration-martingale (handbook/parts/p15/martingales-and-convergence.tex 15-33) defines adaptedness but does not require it of martingales, submartingales or supermartingales. The proofs of thm:p15-submartingale-ui (annex 204-207, F_infinity-measurability of limsup/liminf; annex 219-221, F_n-events for the bracket) and thm:p15-closed-martingale (annex 234-235, X_n F_n-measurable) use it. This packet's owned file handbook/parts/p15/martingales-stopping-and-sequential-random-constructions-w02c-p15-019.tex supplies it in def:p15-w02c-p15-019-adapted-classes (34-53) and names these theorems (486-495); C007 and C009 are covered only with that file routed (route pending).

Citation precision, thm:p15-closed-martingale: the closing-variable identification X_infinity = E(Z|F_infinity) (body 140-142) is followed directly by \cite[lems. 4.6.5--6, thm. 4.6.7]; those items do not contain it (in the source it is the content of Theorem 4.6.8, p. 247). Read as a theorem-level citation the attribution is supported by the chapter locator pp. 244-250; the identification is proved in the annex.

Citation precision, thm:p15-levy-backward: \cite[thm. 4.7.3] (body 354) directly follows the handbook's finite-dimensional extension of all upward and downward limits (body 351-353), which Durrett's Theorem 4.7.3 (p. 250, scalar) does not state; the extension is not marked as supplied by the handbook.

Durrett's title for Theorem 4.6.10, 'Dominated convergence theorem for conditional expectations' (p. 248), is not used on the route; the statement is item 2 of thm:p15-changing-conditional-limits. The name 'Levy's 0-1 law' (Thm 4.6.9) appears only as an index entry (body 175).

Example 4.6.11's preamble (uniform integrability with a.s. convergence gives E(X_n|F) -> E(X|F) in L1, by Thm 4.6.3 and Ex. 4.6.7) is not stated in thm:p15-ui-counterexamples item 3; it follows from thm:p15-vitali-convergence with thm:p15-changing-conditional-limits item 1 for a constant filtration, and item 3 states the L1 convergence for the instance.
The converse in thm:p15-ui-moment-criteria is indexed as the de la Vallee Poussin criterion (body 60) without a source for the eponym.

The source's first step in the proof of Theorem 4.6.1 (P(A_n) -> 0 implies E(|X|;A_n) -> 0 by dominated convergence) is replaced by the tail-splitting estimate (annex 78-79, remark 95-97); a different complete proof.
